mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which is positive for economic growth and thus for S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE is low but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the next 20-day periods, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days when INDPRO growth exceeds 2%.
failure_condition: If INDPRO growth exceeds 2% but S&P 500 returns are not positive in more than 50% of the next 60-day periods, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong demand in the housing market, which is positive for the economy and S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the next 60-day periods, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) combined with low unemployment (UNRATE) may indicate a tight labor market and potential inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS are high and UNRATE is low but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 30% of the next 20-day periods, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth (GDPC1) above 2% indicates a strong economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth exceeds 2% but S&P 500 returns are not positive in more than 50% of the next 60-day periods, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, high federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) may signal monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS are high in a late-cycle expansion but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 30% of the next 20-day periods, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Strong retail sales (RSAFS) indicate high consumer spending, which is positive for the economy and S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS growth is strong but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the next 20-day periods, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL) combined with rising federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) may indicate tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 300 and FEDFUNDS increase by 0.5% in the last month
failure_condition: If CPI is high and FEDFUNDS are rising but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 30% of the next 60-day periods, this hypothesis is rejected.
